query: Our managed environment in eu-west is responding inconsistently today. Is there a current regional incident, and when was its status last updated?

results.content:
## Event summary

Maintenance event `AMS-2023-Q4-NET-17` is a scheduled AWS Management Service
network-control update planned for 18 November 2023 from 02:00 UTC to 04:00
UTC. The change window is expected to affect management-plane actions only. The
notice states that running customer workloads should remain online, but managed
scaling actions, configuration pushes, and health-status propagation may pause
briefly during the event.

metadata.title: Maintenance Notice AMS-2023-Q4-NET-17 for AWS Management Service

results.content:
## Expected impact

During the window, customers may see delayed dashboard status refreshes and up
to two short control-plane interruptions, each not expected to exceed 10
minutes. The event does not call for customer-side service restarts. If a
customer relies on just-in-time infrastructure changes during the window, those
changes should be rescheduled when possible.

metadata.title: Maintenance Notice AMS-2023-Q4-NET-17 for AWS Management Service

results.content:
## What support provides

Support should quote the event ID, planned start and end time, and the managed
service components affected. Updates are posted at event start, every 30
minutes while work remains active, and at completion. If the interruption
exceeds the notice threshold, support opens an incident bridge and posts an
unscheduled-impact update tied to the same event ID.

metadata.title: Maintenance Notice AMS-2023-Q4-NET-17 for AWS Management Service

results.content:
## What the customer provides

Customers usually only need to provide the region or managed environment they
are asking about. If they report a symptom, a timestamp and short impact
description help support compare it with the live status feed.

metadata.title: General AWS Management Service Health and Status Updates

results.content:
## Overview

Use this article for general questions about current platform status, broad
service health summaries, and unscheduled impact notices affecting AWS
Management Service. It is intended for customers asking whether the managed
platform is presently healthy, degraded, or recovering.

metadata.title: General AWS Management Service Health and Status Updates

results.content:
## What support provides

Support can summarize whether the service is operating normally, whether an
unscheduled incident is open, and whether any region-wide degradations are under
investigation. General health updates include the incident state, affected
components, and the time of the last published update.

metadata.title: General AWS Management Service Health and Status Updates

results.content:
## What the customer should do before the window

Customers should review whether any planned deployments, scaling changes, or
configuration edits can be moved outside the maintenance window. For event
`AMS-2023-Q4-NET-17`, support recommends pausing non-urgent management changes
starting six hours before the scheduled start. The customer should confirm their
primary and backup technical contacts, make sure on-call staff know the event
ID and UTC timing, and save current runbooks where the team can reach them
quickly.

If the workload has business-critical transaction periods, the customer should
identify the expected impact if management-plane updates are delayed for up to
10 minutes. A recent read-only export of key configuration records and a
baseline capture of application health are useful because they help the team
recognize whether observed behavior during the window is new.

metadata.title: Customer Preparation and Contingency Planning for Scheduled AWS Maintenance

results.content:
## Escalation

This preparation article is for intermittent latency, not a live outage. If the
customer reports an active service interruption lasting more than 15 minutes, no
current access to core systems, or repeated crashes, route the case to the
operations response team before continuing consultation planning.

metadata.title: Preparing Latency Evidence Before a Server Management Consultation

results.content:
## What support provides

Support confirms whether alerting is enabled on the managed account, records the
threshold values, and states when alerts are evaluated. In this corpus, standard
cost alerts are checked every six hours against accumulated managed-service
spend. Support can also explain how alert recipients are updated if team
ownership changes.

metadata.title: Setting Cost Alert Thresholds for AWS Management Service Accounts

results.content:
## What the customer provides

Ask the customer for the date and approximate time of at least three recent
latency events, which applications or services were affected, and whether the
slowdown was visible to end users or only to administrators. Helpful evidence
includes CPU, memory, disk, and network utilization from the same period;
server role labels; recent patching or deployment activity; and whether the
problem appeared on one system or across a cluster. A brief note about business
impact, such as delayed request handling or missed job windows, helps support
prioritize the consultation.

Customers should gather evidence only through existing dashboards, operating
system counters, or exported logs. They should not change live performance
settings, restart services, or disable protections solely to produce data.

metadata.title: Preparing Latency Evidence Before a Server Management Consultation

query: We are adding a Jira review state and want a specific project role emailed when that transition occurs. Which workflow and mail-routing configurations must be handled separately?

results.content:
## What support provides

Support reviews the notification scheme, watcher settings, and event mapping to
explain why a message was or was not sent. Changes are limited to mail-routing
behavior and recipient scope.

Customers often describe this as a workflow problem because the email is sent
after an issue changes status. Support should still separate the event that
triggered the mail from the workflow step itself before changing any settings.

metadata.title: Notification Schemes and Watchers in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## What support provides

Support reviews the requested workflow map, checks for conflicts with existing
boards and issue screens, and advises whether the change fits native Jira 8.20
workflow capabilities. Standard support can help create new statuses, add or
restrict transitions, and apply clear transition conditions when the approval
rules are already defined. After configuration, support should validate that
issues can still move through the intended path and that no team loses the
ability to complete required work.

Once the before-and-after map and transition rules are complete, support
provides a change estimate. A single-project workflow with defined conditions
normally requires four business days for staging configuration and validation.
Shared workflows or dynamic rules require specialist review before a timeline
or plugin need can be confirmed. These are support-owned conclusions, not
details the customer is expected to supply.

metadata.title: Adding Workflow Statuses and Transition Conditions in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## Dynamic behavior and limits

When a customer asks for issue handling to shift dynamically as project goals
change, support should narrow the request to explicit rules rather than vague
optimization. Jira can enforce named statuses and documented transition
conditions, but it cannot infer business priority without a defined policy
matrix. This article does not cover notification changes or permission-scheme
design. Escalate when multiple projects share one workflow and the requested
change would affect teams outside the customer's approved scope.

metadata.title: Adding Workflow Statuses and Transition Conditions in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## What the customer provides

Support should ask for the current workflow name, the issue types affected, and
a simple before-and-after list of statuses and allowed transitions. If the
customer wants transitions to depend on priority, approval, or issue state, the
exact rule must be supplied in business language so it can be translated into
workflow conditions without guessing. A staging project or test window is also
important because workflow changes can affect active teams immediately.

The customer does not need to predefine every Jira configuration detail, but
they do need to state which statuses should be added, removed, or repurposed.

metadata.title: Adding Workflow Statuses and Transition Conditions in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## What the customer provides

Support should ask which project is affected, which event sends the unwanted or
missing email, and which users or roles are expected to receive it. If the
customer references a custom workflow, support still needs the notification
scheme name separately because the scheme and the workflow are different objects.

metadata.title: Notification Schemes and Watchers in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## Overview

This article supports Jira 8.20 requests to add statuses, modify transitions,
or align workflow conditions with a new ticket handling policy. It is commonly
retrieved alongside the custom priority article because teams often need both
sets of changes to reflect a revised issue process.

metadata.title: Adding Workflow Statuses and Transition Conditions in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not tell the customer how to redesign statuses, transitions,
or priority levels. Those changes require separate workflow guidance.

metadata.title: Project Permissions and Role Access in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## What support provides

Support checks the permission scheme, associated project roles, and whether the
problem is caused by missing membership or by a separate workflow condition.
Support may correct role assignments or permission mappings when the change is
approved.

The customer does not need to know the exact permission key names in advance.
They do need to describe the blocked action clearly so support can tell whether
the issue is access-related or part of the workflow design.

metadata.title: Project Permissions and Role Access in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## Overview

Use this article when a Jira 8.20 customer needs help with who can browse,
create, transition, edit, or administer issues in a project. Permission-scheme
questions often sound similar to workflow requests but are controlled
independently.

metadata.title: Project Permissions and Role Access in Jira Software 8.20

results.content:
## What support provides

Support confirms that Jira 8.20 can host a revised priority scheme without a
plugin for the core priority field itself. Before implementation, support
advises taking a configuration snapshot and testing the new values in staging
when available. The normal sequence is to create or rename priority values,
confirm their display order, map any dependent boards or filters that reference
old names, and then verify that issue creation and search still behave as
expected.

If the customer asks for dynamic reprioritization tied to project state or
business goals, support should treat that as a second decision point. Basic
priority changes are straightforward; automatic priority changes require an
approved ruleset and separate review of whether native automation already in
place can support it.

metadata.title: Custom Priority Configuration in Jira Software 8.20

query: Our router order is still editable: we need to change its destination and find out whether expedited service remains available after the update.

results.content:
## What support provides

Support can update the address only before carrier handoff. Once the package has
been manifested and transferred to the carrier, the original address must remain
in place unless the carrier separately approves a reroute request. Support
should tell the customer whether the order is still editable and whether the
change will delay dispatch.

metadata.title: Shipping Address Change Requests for Hardware Orders

results.content:
## What the customer provides

Support needs the order number, the requested new address, and confirmation of
whether the order has already shipped. If the destination change affects tax or
export screening, the customer may also be asked to reconfirm billing details.

metadata.title: Shipping Address Change Requests for Hardware Orders

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not estimate delivery timelines for a future purchase and does
not create tracking numbers before shipment.

metadata.title: Shipping Address Change Requests for Hardware Orders

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not authorize shipping-address changes after carrier handoff
and does not define the return window if the product is unsuitable. Those are
separate processes with different requirements.

metadata.title: Shipping Methods and Tracking for Networking Equipment Orders

results.content:
## Overview

Use this article when a customer wants to change the delivery address on an
existing hardware order. This process is separate from quoting shipping speed,
tracking a package, or explaining the return window.

metadata.title: Shipping Address Change Requests for Hardware Orders

results.content:
## What support provides

Support checks inventory status, confirms which shipping methods are available
for the destination, and explains the quoted transit range. Once the order is
dispatched, tracking details are normally posted to the order record within 24
hours and can also be sent by email on request. If multiple packages are used,
support explains which items are in each shipment.

Support should also explain that quoted delivery windows assume the order clears
verification before the daily cutoff. If stock must be moved between warehouses,
the customer should be told that dispatch timing may shift by one business day
even when the selected carrier service remains the same. For time-sensitive
projects, support can note whether split shipment is available so essential
hardware can leave first and accessories can follow.

metadata.title: Shipping Methods and Tracking for Networking Equipment Orders

results.content:
## Standard timelines

For in-stock hardware, standard ground delivery is quoted at five to seven
business days from order release. Expedited delivery is two to three business
days, and priority overnight service is available in eligible metro regions for
orders cleared before the daily cutoff. Delivery commitments begin after order
verification and payment approval, not when the cart is created or the inquiry
is sent.

metadata.title: Shipping Methods and Tracking for Networking Equipment Orders

results.content:
## What support provides

Support can confirm whether the requested upgrade path is within the internally
approved software family, whether an intermediate release is required, and what
pre-change checks are expected. The normal advice is to save the running
configuration, verify console access, and schedule the change during a controlled
window.

metadata.title: Firmware Planning Limits for Cisco ISR4331 Routers

results.content:
## What the customer provides

The customer should provide the channels where requests currently arrive, the
main categories of work they want tracked, and how they want urgent versus
routine issues distinguished. If they already use approval steps, escalation
paths, or service targets, those should be shared as part of intake. For teams
that mention upgrade handling, support also needs to know whether upgrades are
approved in one queue, in a separate change flow, or outside the ticketing
system today.

The customer does not need to propose a final workflow diagram. The point of
discovery is to uncover it.

metadata.title: Discovery Inputs for Ticketing Workflow Recommendations

results.content:
## What the customer provides

To quote a realistic delivery window, support needs the destination region,
whether the order is shipping to a business or residential address, and whether
the customer wants standard, expedited, or priority service. The customer does
not need a tracking number before the order has shipped.

metadata.title: Shipping Methods and Tracking for Networking Equipment Orders

query: A recently delivered QN90A flickers on internal menus. We need safe diagnostic steps and a comparison of the still-open store-return route with manufacturer technician service.

results.content:
## What support provides

Support interprets the results. If flicker persists on the built-in menu,
continues after a clean power cycle, and is unaffected by input changes, support
should treat the case as a likely hardware-path issue that needs warranty
routing or technician assessment. If the flicker happens only with one source,
support can narrow the next step to cabling or source configuration rather than
the display assembly.

metadata.title: Safe Troubleshooting for Intermittent Flicker on Samsung QN90A TVs

results.content:
## Limits and escalation

Do not ask the customer to remove the back cover, press on the panel, reseat
internal boards, or repeatedly factory-reset the unit. Escalate to authorized
service when the symptom persists after the safe checks above, when the screen
shows flicker before any external source is selected, or when the problem has
become more frequent over time.

metadata.title: Safe Troubleshooting for Intermittent Flicker on Samsung QN90A TVs

results.content:
## Safe checks the customer can perform

Ask the customer to note whether the flicker appears on every source or only on
one device. A useful first check is opening the TV home menu or a built-in app;
if flicker is visible there as well, the problem is less likely to be caused by
an external cable or player. For external sources, the customer can reseat the
HDMI cable, try a known-good cable, and temporarily set the source output to a
standard refresh rate such as 60 Hz.

The customer may also power the TV off, unplug it for one minute, and reconnect
it directly to a wall outlet if it was previously attached to a power strip.
Picture settings that aggressively alter brightness can be turned off for
testing, including contrast enhancer and motion smoothing. These checks are safe
because they are reversible and do not require service access.

metadata.title: Safe Troubleshooting for Intermittent Flicker on Samsung QN90A TVs

results.content:
## Symptoms

Use this article when a Samsung QN90A owner reports intermittent screen
flicker, brightness pulsing, or rapid flashing that disrupts viewing. The goal
is to separate input-related behavior from a likely panel or control-board issue
without asking the customer to open the television or perform unsafe hardware
work.

metadata.title: Safe Troubleshooting for Intermittent Flicker on Samsung QN90A TVs

results.content:
## What support provides

Support interprets the results and decides whether the next step is audio
configuration review, accessory isolation, or hardware service for the audio
path. Picture flicker, backlight pulsing, and display artifacts are outside the
scope of this article.

metadata.title: Troubleshooting Audio Dropouts on Samsung QN90A Televisions

results.content:
## Limits

Do not use audio troubleshooting as evidence that the panel itself is defective.
If the customer reports flashing images, menu flicker, or brightness pulsing,
move the case to the display-troubleshooting flow instead of continuing with
speaker or eARC checks.

metadata.title: Troubleshooting Audio Dropouts on Samsung QN90A Televisions

results.content:
## What the customer provides

The customer should provide the model, serial number, purchase date, seller
name, and proof of purchase. For intermittent display problems, a short photo or
video clip is helpful, along with notes about which sources were tested and
whether the built-in menu also flickers. The customer may also be asked to
confirm that the screen is free of impact cracks, liquid exposure, and
unauthorized repair attempts.

The customer is not expected to diagnose the failed part or to decide whether
the issue is covered.

metadata.title: Warranty Routing and Technician Assessment for Samsung Television Display Defects

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not determine manufacturer warranty coverage, authorize field
technician visits, or diagnose flicker symptoms. Once the store return window
has passed, the request moves to the hardware warranty process.

metadata.title: Retail Return Windows for Samsung Televisions Purchased Through the Store

results.content:
## Safe checks

Ask the customer whether the dropout occurs with internal streaming apps, an
HDMI source, or only when a soundbar is connected. Safe checks include reseating
the HDMI cable, temporarily disabling eARC for testing, switching the digital
audio output format, and testing the TV speakers directly. If the issue appears
only on one external device, support should narrow the investigation to that
source path.

metadata.title: Troubleshooting Audio Dropouts on Samsung QN90A Televisions

results.content:
## Symptoms

Use this article when sound cuts out, crackles, or falls out of sync on a
Samsung QN90A while the picture remains stable. Common retrieval language
includes audio interruption, sound dropout, eARC instability, and intermittent
volume loss.

metadata.title: Troubleshooting Audio Dropouts on Samsung QN90A Televisions

query: Can you enroll a new hardware security key for multifactor authentication and revoke the employee's lost authenticator?

results.content:
## Eligibility

Standard hardware returns are accepted within 30 calendar days of delivery when
the customer requests a return merchandise authorization, or RMA, and the unit
is returned with its original major components. Open-box returns are allowed,
but missing modules, damaged ports, or altered serial labels move the case to
manual review. Compatibility disappointment by itself does not guarantee a full
refund if the product was sold correctly to the documented specification.

metadata.title: Return Eligibility and RMA Process for Networking Hardware

results.content:
## What support provides

Support validates the identity check, issues the reset, and notes whether the
customer must update multifactor settings at the next sign-in. If the identity
record does not match, support routes the request to account recovery review.

metadata.title: Identity Checks for Account Password Reset Requests

results.content:
## What support provides

Support confirms whether the request is inside the return window, issues the RMA
identifier, and explains where the item must be shipped. If restocking applies,
support states it before the return is finalized. Once the returned hardware is
received and passes inspection, support closes the RMA and releases the refund
or replacement outcome tied to the order type.

When the customer is asking before purchase, support can explain that the RMA
process exists without predicting the final inspection outcome in advance.
Returned hardware is checked for missing accessories, altered serial labels, and
obvious port damage before the case is completed. If inspection finds a mismatch
with the submitted return reason, support documents that difference for the
customer rather than silently reducing the outcome.

metadata.title: Return Eligibility and RMA Process for Networking Hardware

results.content:
## Overview

Use this article when a customer cannot access an account and needs a password
reset. The focus is verifying identity safely before support changes login
credentials.

metadata.title: Identity Checks for Account Password Reset Requests

results.content:
## What the customer provides

The customer should provide the account identifier, current contact email, and
one approved identity-check detail such as the last successful billing postcode
or the name of the authorized signer on file. Support should not ask for full
payment card numbers or plaintext passwords.

metadata.title: Identity Checks for Account Password Reset Requests

results.content:
## Overview

This article covers return requests for networking hardware after delivery. It
is appropriate when a customer asks what happens if a router or similar product
does not meet expectations and wants to understand the support process before
ordering.

metadata.title: Return Eligibility and RMA Process for Networking Hardware

results.content:
## What the customer provides

The customer should provide the order number, delivery date, model, serial
number if available, and the reason for return. If the package arrived damaged,
photos of the carton and contents are helpful. The customer is not expected to
create the RMA code on their own.

metadata.title: Return Eligibility and RMA Process for Networking Hardware

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not approve billing adjustments, cancel hardware orders in
transit, or act as a return authorization. If the customer is actually disputing
a charge or returning equipment, support should move to the correct policy
process.

metadata.title: Intake for Subscription Cancellation Requests

results.content:
## Compatibility notes

The ISR4331 is most often recommended for branch aggregation, managed VPN edge,
and mixed voice-data office routing. Customers should confirm whether they need
additional modules for serial handoff, LTE backup, or dense switch-port
expansion, because those capabilities are not included in the base chassis.
Support can clarify catalog compatibility and licensed feature families, but it
does not design the customer's full network from this reference article alone.

When a customer asks about unique features, support can describe the modular
expansion bays, encrypted branch connectivity profile, and central policy use
case in plain language. If the customer already knows the WAN handoff type and
uplink redundancy requirement, support can also tell them whether the base
chassis is sufficient or whether an approved module must be added to the quote.

metadata.title: Cisco ISR4331 Specification and Compatibility Reference

results.content:
## Limits

This article does not unlock suspended contracts, change billing contacts, or
override identity controls because the caller says access is urgent. Escalate
only when the customer no longer controls the registered email and standard
identity verification cannot be completed safely.

metadata.title: Identity Checks for Account Password Reset Requests
